profile.campus: Switch Citadel Campus, Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada
profile.reading:
This building is real, it has a name, and the Storey County assessor supplies both. The parcel containing this record's coordinates is 005-012-35, situs 5 Superloop Circle, McCarran, Nevada 89437, on 23.88 acres, zoned I2, in tax district 122 industrial, inside the Tahoe-Reno Industrial General Improvement District. Its registered owner is NV RNO 5, LLC, with mail directed to Switch, Ltd, Attention Legal Department, 7135 South Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas. The county's own personal property account for the parcel gives its location as 1 Superloop Circle, Reno 5, McCarran. An earlier version of this entry could not confirm that a building called Tahoe Reno 5 existed as anything other than a mapping label extrapolated from a sequence. The county record settles it.

The assessor describes the main structure as NAP 05, an industrial building of 478,454 square feet total floor area with a year built of 2025. Switch calls its data halls NAPs, for network access point, so NAP 05 and Tahoe Reno 5 are the same building under the operator's and the assessor's naming. The record lists concrete tilt up exterior walls, complete heating, cooling and ventilation across 100 percent of the floor area with two climate zones, sprinklers across 100 percent, one freight elevator with two stops, and a fire alarm system covering the full 478,454 square feet. A second record covers site improvements dated 2026, including 345 square feet of substations, 91,961 square feet of reinforced concrete flatwork, an 842 square foot mechanical penthouse dated 2025, a 2,673 square foot concrete truck ramp and 9,168 square feet of concrete wall.

The parcel itself is new. It was created in 2024 from parent parcels 005-012-32 and 005-081-10 under parcel map 2024-23, in section 14, township 19 north, range 22 east. A chain of quitclaim deeds recorded on 16 August 2024 moved it from NV TRO 1 and 2 LLC through DB Sunshine Mezz A LLC, Switch Bighorn TK Pledgor LLC and Switch Bighorn TK Holdco LLC to NV RNO 5 LLC, following June 2024 conveyances involving SUPERNAP Reno LLC and Switch, Ltd. The tax roll traces the building coming out of the ground: $75,597.16 for fiscal 2024 to 2025, $307,957.03 for 2025 to 2026, and $1,280,203.57 for 2026 to 2027 at a rate of 3.4607, paid in quarterly installments by Switch. Current taxable value is $7,541,543 of land and $98,151,654 of building, $105,693,197 in total, assessed at $36,992,619, with $27,774,648 of that recorded as new construction this year.

On power, care is needed. Switch's own campus page describes the Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and gigawatts of capacity at completion, with up to 2 MW per cabinet, and none of that is a figure for this building. No IT load, utility service capacity or standby generation rating is published for Tahoe Reno 5. The 345 square feet of substations in the county record is a structure's footprint, not a capacity. Switch's July 2020 announcement with Capital Dynamics put its Gigawatt 1 programme at 555 MW of solar and 800 MWh of storage across Clark and Storey counties, the largest behind the meter component being 127 MW of solar with 240 MWh of storage in Storey County, and stated that Switch power costs would stay in the range of 5 cents a kilowatt hour on 100 percent renewable power. That is a campus and company level arrangement, and this registry does not attach any of it to this building's meter.

What is not known: the building's IT load, its utility service capacity, its diesel standby rating, whether it takes bundled NV Energy service or is served under Nevada's large customer departure regime, and which of the campus generation resources actually sit behind its meter.

profile.community_note: The tax roll for this parcel is a legible record of a building being built. The bill was $75,597.16 for fiscal 2024 to 2025, $307,957.03 for 2025 to 2026 and $1,280,203.57 for 2026 to 2027, and $27,774,648 of new construction was added to the roll in the current year. Local school funding rises with it, with $277,444.64 of operating and $53,528.32 of debt levy attributable to this single parcel for 2026 to 2027, against $1,889.53 reaching the Storey County general fund. The parcel was carved out of the wider Switch holding in 2024 and conveyed through a chain of quitclaim deeds recorded on 16 August 2024 ending at NV RNO 5 LLC.
profile.incentives_note: The parcel pays a full unabated bill, but almost three quarters of it is redirected. Of the $1,280,203.57 billed for fiscal 2026 to 2027, the county taxing body table assigns $937,124.43 to a line it labels TIA PIPELINE TIF, $277,444.64 to school operating and $53,528.32 to school debt, $7,675.88 to the state, $1,889.53 to the county general fund, $914.54 to Fire District 474, $554.71 each to capital projects and roads, $369.81 to capital acquisition, and small amounts to industrial accident, industrial medical and youth services. TIA is a tax increment area. Storey County approved a tax increment area to repay the companies that fronted the cost of the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center effluent pipeline, a 13 mile line bringing up to 4,000 acre feet a year of treated wastewater from the Truckee Meadows Water Reclamation Facility in Sparks, after an earlier $35 million state backed bond package collapsed. The county tax roll does not state which tax increment area the line refers to, so that identification is by name rather than by an explicit statement in the record.

The parcel is 005-012-35, zoned I2, in tax district 122 industrial, within the Tahoe-Reno Industrial General Improvement District, legally described as a portion of section 14, township 19 north, range 22 east, created under parcel map 2024-23 in 2024 from parent parcels 005-012-32 and 005-081-10. The county land use code is 501, general industrial, still flagged under construction on the current roll.

Those are campus and company level figures. This registry does not attribute any of that generation to this building meter, and does not record an onsite_generation_mw for this row.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 5 is a 478,454 square foot data center built in 2025 on 23.88 acres in Storey County, Nevada, owned by NV RNO 5 LLC and operated by Switch. The building is real and verified by county assessor records as NAP 05, completed as a climate-controlled industrial structure with full mechanical systems, fire suppression and dual climate zones. No power capacity is published for this building under any metric—not IT load, not utility service capacity, not standby generation. The county record notes 345 square feet of substations on the parcel, a footprint measurement that carries no megawatt value.

Switch operates the wider Tahoe Reno campus as part of its Gigawatt programme, which announced 127 MW of solar and 240 MWh of battery storage in Storey County in July 2020, and stated power costs in the range of 5 cents per kilowatt hour on renewable power. That is a campus-wide figure across multiple buildings and an operational target, not an attributed capacity for Tahoe Reno 5 itself. Which generation resources, if any, sit behind this building's meter is not published. The building holds Switch's proprietary Tier 5 Platinum rating, a designation for facilities meeting Switch's own standards; no third-party certification is listed.

Among Nevada's 26 mapped data center facilities, only 2 publish power capacity figures and those total 10.37 MW, a number dwarfed by major out-of-state hubs. Tahoe Reno 5 ranks third among the state's published capacity sites, though it contributes zero to that state total because no figure is released. The building is fully taxed without abatement, with $1.28 million billed for fiscal 2026-27, of which 73 percent flows to a tax increment area funding regional infrastructure and 22 percent to schools. The facility is new enough that its contribution to state AI infrastructure cannot be read from public specifications.
